turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs Kearney, I've your blood pressure here before you go in. It's 132 over 84, pulse 78, and your temperature is 36.7. Grand, the doctor will be with you now.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come on in, Mrs Kearney, and you too. I'm Dr O'Brien. What has you in today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. I am sorry to trouble you. I have this burning again when I pass water.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ah, I'm sorry you're dealing with that. Tell me a bit about it, in your own words.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): It stings something awful at the end of the stream. This is the third time this year, Doctor.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Well, actually, maybe the fourth. I had forgotten the one after Christmas.
[SEG0007] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was up half the night with it, Doctor. I made her come in. The traffic on the M50 was desperate, mind you.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair play to you for coming. How long has this particular bout been going on?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Since Monday, so that would be four days now. I have to go very often, and there is an urgency to it.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And when you do go, is there much there, or just a little?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Only a small amount, I am afraid, and it burns the whole way.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the urine at all?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor, I have not seen any blood.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about pain in your back, or up in the side?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. It is mostly the burning when I pass water.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. And have you felt feverish, or shivery?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No, I have not had a temperature. I feel a little tired, but nothing dramatic.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vaginal discharge, or itching, or soreness down below? I have to ask, I'm afraid.
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. Nothing of that nature. I would rather not discuss it, if you do not mind.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mam, you were saying last night...
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Well. I am embarrassed, but there has been a little irritation on the outside. I should have said so. Not an itch exactly, more a raw feeling.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's alright, thank you for telling me. Any discharge with that?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose there might be a tiny bit. Sometimes, not really. I could not be sure.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll leave that as uncertain, so. Have you taken anything for this?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): I am afraid I did something unwise. I took some of my sister's leftover capsules, the yellow and black ones she had for a urine infection.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you know the name of them?

[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): I do not, I am sorry. They were those urine capsules. I think the dose was one hundred milligrams, one twice a day, by mouth, for three days. Then they ran out and I stopped, two days ago.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The box in her bathroom said something like Macrobid, Doctor, but I only glanced at it. I wouldn't swear to it.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's grand, we'll not hang a name on it if you're not sure. Are you on any regular medicines?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Only my blood pressure tablet, the little white one, in the morning. I forget the proper name. Five milligrams, I believe.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): And how is your stomach? Any nausea, or pain in the tummy?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): No nausea, Doctor, and no tummy pain. Passing water is the only trouble, apart from that irritation.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): This does sound like another bladder infection, a cystitis, though I'd like the urine to confirm it. We'll send a sample off today.
[SEG0034] person_1 (NURSE): I can take the midstream sample now, Doctor, and we'll send it for culture.

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Perfect. Mrs Kearney, drink plenty of water, and please don't use anyone else's tablets again. If you're not easier in three days, or if you get a fever or pain in the back, come straight back to me.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. I will do exactly as you say. Good afternoon.
